macro_blurb: Today's tape is shaped by a mix of corporate restructuring, capital-markets supply, and trade diplomacy rather than central-bank action. In US tech, Intuit announced a roughly 17% workforce reduction citing slowing growth, while SpaceX filed for what would be a record IPO despite disclosing billion-dollar losses in its prospectus — a notable test of appetite for large new equity supply. Jeff Bezos used a CNBC interview to defend billionaires, promote AI and praise Donald Trump, keeping the AI-and-policy narrative in focus alongside reports of attorneys urging Congress to block a Trump "lawfare" fund. For European and UK-linked names, Britain sealed a £3.7bn trade deal with six Gulf states, while a sinkhole shutting a LaGuardia runway adds localized US airline disruption.
synthesis:
Today's screen is unambiguous: income and value, anchored in Europe. Eight of ten picks are EU-listed, the average Yield percentile sits at 89.8 and Value at 83.2, while Quality is the laggard at 72.5 — and that's before noting that 1COV.DE and HPQ don't even carry a Quality score. Seven of the ten names yield above 5.7%, and trailing P/Es cluster between 7x and 17x against sector medians roughly double that. No single sector dominates — Financials and Utilities tie at two each — but the factor signature is consistent: cheap European cash-return.

The clearest thread runs through EDEN.PA, TEP.PA and SCR.PA — French names trading at 7-10x earnings with FCF yields of 15-24% and dividend yields near 6%, each carrying a top-decile momentum score as the tape rewards the deep-value reset. Separately, ENG.MC and VER.VI form a regulated-utility pair, but with opposite risk profiles: Enagás delivers a 5.91% yield on a 0.1% FCF yield and 118 debt/equity, while Verbund's 18 debt/equity and 13.5% ROE come at 2x book. With the macro driven by corporate supply (SpaceX IPO, Intuit cuts) rather than rates, the yield trade has room.

The outlier is 1COV.DE — a loss-making chemicals name riding ADNOC deal mechanics, not fundamentals. Conspicuously absent: Healthcare, Energy, Real Estate and Consumer Cyclical from 992 screened. Watch the ADNOC/Covestro EU concession ruling and the £3.7bn UK-Gulf trade deal — both can reprice these names inside two weeks.
